answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on work. Whether an agent models ember spread, maps tundra or surveys a ridge, the same bond applies, and a public fraud proof can trigger its forfeiture. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month; using them to submit provably fraudulent results risks losing that capital, making disposable identities costly.
